title: How do QR codes store information?
sources: Denso Wave Invention of QR Code

lines.text: How can a tiny square of random black and white pixels beam a website link to your camera in half a second?
lines.caps: How does a *QR code | store data in black and *white?

lines.text: Invented in nineteen ninety-four to track auto parts in Japan, QR stands for Quick Response.
lines.caps: Invented by Toyota to track *parts | at lightning *speed

lines.text: Those three large squares in the corners are position markers that tell your phone camera orientation and angle.
lines.caps: Three corner squares tell *cameras | the exact orientation and *tilt

lines.text: The smaller square near the bottom right aligns the image to correct distortion.
The remaining grid of pixels encodes characters into binary ones and zeros.
lines.caps: The pixel grid encodes *characters | into binary ones and *zeros

lines.text: Even better, QR codes feature Reed-Solomon error correction, meaning they scan perfectly even if thirty percent is ripped or dirty.
lines.caps: Scans perfectly even if *30% | is ripped or *dirty!

lines.text: A simple two-dimensional barcode connects the physical world to the digital universe.
lines.caps: Connecting the physical *world | to the internet in a *snap!
